title: THE PHASE ROTOR
briefing: The grid's oldest generator is a three-phase rotor with coils in phase R, G and B. A shift pulls one coil out of each of two phases and winds both into the third. The coils never leave the rotor. If all of them ever pile into a single phase, the rotor locks and tears its bearings apart.
solutions: 9 - r - g = b && g mod 3 != r mod 3

intro: A ROTOR THAT TURNS COILS INTO OTHER COILS. ALCHEMY WITH COPPER.

default: The phases climb and fall by different amounts. Look at how they differ, not how big they are.
Every shift moves the gap between two phases by a whole number of steps of the same size. Which size?
Read each gap through the right MOD. More than one gap may need watching.
